# nrsc5

**HD Radio (NRSC-5) receiver for an RTL-SDR -- the digital side of North American FM and AM**

- **Version recorded:** 3.2.0
- **Categories:** `broadcast`
- **Upstream:** <https://github.com/theori-io/nrsc5>

## What it does

nrsc5 receives HD Radio, the in-band digital broadcast used by FM and AM stations in the United States and some other parts of North America (the NRSC-5 standard), from an RTL-SDR dongle, and plays it. Give it a station's frequency and a program number -- 0 is the main program, and upstream's usage takes 0 to 3 -- and it decodes the digital audio to the sound card or to a WAV file, and prints what the station sends alongside: station name, song title and artist, and the station's emergency alerts. It can also save the files the station transmits beside the audio, such as album art (`--dump-aas-files`), read from an `rtl_tcp` server on the network (`-H`), or decode a recording instead of a live dongle (`-r`). Receive only.

## Why you would want it

The catalog had DAB twice (`welle-io`, `dablin`) and HD Radio not at all, and HD Radio is the digital broadcast standard a North American listener can actually hear. A station's second and third programs (HD2, HD3) exist only in digital and are not heard on an analog radio at all. It is the reference open decoder; GUIs such as NRSC5 Studio and SDR programs with HD Radio plug-ins build on its library, and none of those is carried.

## Before it will work

An RTL-SDR dongle and an FM antenna, and the dongle's permissions (the `rtl-sdr` hardware entry's `plugdev` group). A sound device for live listening; `-o file.wav` needs none. A station in range that broadcasts HD Radio: outside North America there is usually none, and nrsc5 reports nothing rather than an error.

## Known problems

**It needs the whole dongle**: like every librtlsdr program it cannot share the device with gqrx, readsb or another decoder running at the same time. HD Radio is weaker than the analog signal it rides beside, so a station that plays clearly on FM can still lose digital synchronisation indoors; it logs "Lost synchronization" and recovers when the signal does. Set the dongle's frequency error with `-p` if it is more than a few PPM out. `-h` is not an option; the usage line it prints in reply lists them all. **`--dump-aas-files` is marked "insecure" in upstream's own README**: it writes files into the directory you give, named from what the station transmits (`src/main.c` builds the path from the broadcast name). Give it an empty directory of its own, or leave it off.
What was measured: built on Debian 13 and Kali, and on both decoded upstream's own recorded sample (`support/sample.xz`, read with `-r`): it synchronised, printed the station name, two audio programs and their titles, and wrote 2 MB of audio. Not measured: a live dongle, a real station, sound output, the image dumps or `rtl_tcp`.

## Keeping it current

- probe: github tags (`theori-io/nrsc5`)
- strategy: rebuild
- Upstream has tagged three to four times a year since 2025 (v3.0 2025-05, v3.1.0 2025-12, v3.2.0 2026-06). Move the tag and its commit together; check whether the FAAD2 tag in CMakeLists.txt moved with it, and if so take the new tag's archive hash -- the patch must name the tag upstream builds.
